nodes.Name: ScanState
nodes.DocComment:
ScanState represents the scanner state passed to custom scanners.
Scanners may do rune-at-a-time scanning or ask the ScanState
to discover the next space-delimited token.

nodes.Name: Scanner
nodes.DocComment:
Scanner is implemented by any value that has a Scan method, which scans
the input for the representation of a value and stores the result in the
receiver, which must be a pointer to be useful. The Scan method is called
for any argument to [Scan], [Scanf], or [Scanln] that implements it.

nodes.Name: Scan
nodes.DocComment:
Scan scans text read from standard input, storing successive
space-separated values into successive arguments. Newlines count
as space. It returns the number of items successfully scanned.
If that is less than the number of arguments, err will report why.

nodes.Name: Scanln
nodes.DocComment:
Scanln is similar to [Scan], but stops scanning at a newline and
after the final item there must be a newline or EOF.

nodes.Name: Scanf
nodes.DocComment:
Scanf scans text read from standard input, storing successive
space-separated values into successive arguments as determined by
the format. It returns the number of items successfully scanned.
If that is less than the number of arguments, err will report why.
Newlines in the input must match newlines in the format.
The one exception: the verb %c always scans the next rune in the
input, even if it is a space (or tab etc.) or newline.

nodes.Name: Sscan
nodes.DocComment:
Sscan scans the argument string, storing successive space-separated
values into successive arguments. Newlines count as space. It
returns the number of items successfully scanned. If that is less
than the number of arguments, err will report why.

nodes.Name: Sscanln
nodes.DocComment:
Sscanln is similar to [Sscan], but stops scanning at a newline and
after the final item there must be a newline or EOF.

nodes.Name: Sscanf
nodes.DocComment:
Sscanf scans the argument string, storing successive space-separated
values into successive arguments as determined by the format. It
returns the number of items successfully parsed.
Newlines in the input must match newlines in the format.

nodes.Name: Fscan
nodes.DocComment:
Fscan scans text read from r, storing successive space-separated
values into successive arguments. Newlines count as space. It
returns the number of items successfully scanned. If that is less
than the number of arguments, err will report why.

nodes.Name: Fscanln
nodes.DocComment:
Fscanln is similar to [Fscan], but stops scanning at a newline and
after the final item there must be a newline or EOF.

nodes.Name: Fscanf
nodes.DocComment:
Fscanf scans text read from r, storing successive space-separated
values into successive arguments as determined by the format. It
returns the number of items successfully parsed.
Newlines in the input must match newlines in the format.

nodes.Name: scanError
nodes.DocComment:
scanError represents an error generated by the scanning software.
It's used as a unique signature to identify such errors when recovering.

nodes.Name: ss
nodes.DocComment: ss is the internal implementation of ScanState.

nodes.Name: ssave
nodes.DocComment:
ssave holds the parts of ss that need to be
saved and restored on recursive scans.

Fields.Name: validSave
Fields.DocComment: is or was a part of an actual ss.

Fields.Name: nlIsSpace
Fields.DocComment: whether newline counts as white space

Fields.Name: argLimit
Fields.DocComment: max value of ss.count for this arg; argLimit <= limit

nodes.Name: Read
nodes.DocComment:
The Read method is only in ScanState so that ScanState
satisfies io.Reader. It will never be called when used as
intended, so there is no need to make it actually work.

nodes.Name: getRune
nodes.DocComment:
The public method returns an error; this private one panics.
If getRune reaches EOF, the return value is EOF (-1).

nodes.Name: mustReadRune
nodes.DocComment:
mustReadRune turns io.EOF into a panic(io.ErrUnexpectedEOF).
It is called in cases such as string scanning where an EOF is a
syntax error.

nodes.Name: space
nodes.DocComment:
space is a copy of the unicode.White_Space ranges,
to avoid depending on package unicode.

nodes.Name: notSpace
nodes.DocComment: notSpace is the default scanning function used in Token.

nodes.Name: readRune
nodes.DocComment:
readRune is a structure to enable reading UTF-8 encoded code points
from an io.Reader. It is used if the Reader given to the scanner does
not already implement io.RuneScanner.

Fields.Name: pending
Fields.DocComment: number of bytes in pendBuf; only >0 for bad UTF-8

Fields.Name: peekRune
Fields.DocComment: if >=0 next rune; when <0 is ^(previous Rune)

nodes.Name: readByte
nodes.DocComment:
readByte returns the next byte from the input, which may be
left over from a previous read if the UTF-8 was ill-formed.

nodes.Name: ReadRune
nodes.DocComment:
ReadRune returns the next UTF-8 encoded code point from the
io.Reader inside r.

nodes.Name: newScanState
nodes.DocComment: newScanState allocates a new ss struct or grab a cached one.

nodes.Name: free
nodes.DocComment: free saves used ss structs in ssFree; avoid an allocation per invocation.

nodes.Name: SkipSpace
nodes.DocComment:
SkipSpace provides Scan methods the ability to skip space and newline
characters in keeping with the current scanning mode set by format strings
and [Scan]/[Scanln].

nodes.Name: token
nodes.DocComment:
token returns the next space-delimited string from the input. It
skips white space. For Scanln, it stops at newlines. For Scan,
newlines are treated as spaces.

nodes.Name: consume
nodes.DocComment:
consume reads the next rune in the input and reports whether it is in the ok string.
If accept is true, it puts the character into the input token.

nodes.Name: peek
nodes.DocComment: peek reports whether the next character is in the ok string, without consuming it.

nodes.Name: accept
nodes.DocComment:
accept checks the next rune in the input. If it's a byte (sic) in the string, it puts it in the
buffer and returns true. Otherwise it return false.

nodes.Name: okVerb
nodes.DocComment: okVerb verifies that the verb is present in the list, setting s.err appropriately if not.

nodes.Name: scanBool
nodes.DocComment: scanBool returns the value of the boolean represented by the next token.

nodes.Name: binaryDigits
nodes.DocComment: Numerical elements

nodes.Name: octalDigits
nodes.DocComment: Numerical elements

nodes.Name: decimalDigits
nodes.DocComment: Numerical elements

nodes.Name: hexadecimalDigits
nodes.DocComment: Numerical elements

nodes.Name: sign
nodes.DocComment: Numerical elements

nodes.Name: period
nodes.DocComment: Numerical elements

nodes.Name: exponent
nodes.DocComment: Numerical elements

nodes.Name: getBase
nodes.DocComment: getBase returns the numeric base represented by the verb and its digit string.

nodes.Name: scanNumber
nodes.DocComment: scanNumber returns the numerical string with specified digits starting here.

nodes.Name: scanRune
nodes.DocComment: scanRune returns the next rune value in the input.

nodes.Name: scanBasePrefix
nodes.DocComment:
scanBasePrefix reports whether the integer begins with a base prefix
and returns the base, digit string, and whether a zero was found.
It is called only if the verb is %v.

nodes.Name: scanInt
nodes.DocComment:
scanInt returns the value of the integer represented by the next
token, checking for overflow. Any error is stored in s.err.

nodes.Name: scanUint
nodes.DocComment:
scanUint returns the value of the unsigned integer represented
by the next token, checking for overflow. Any error is stored in s.err.

nodes.Name: floatToken
nodes.DocComment:
floatToken returns the floating-point number starting here, no longer than swid
if the width is specified. It's not rigorous about syntax because it doesn't check that
we have at least some digits, but Atof will do that.

nodes.Name: complexTokens
nodes.DocComment:
complexTokens returns the real and imaginary parts of the complex number starting here.
The number might be parenthesized and has the format (N+Ni) where N is a floating-point
number and there are no spaces within.

nodes.Name: convertFloat
nodes.DocComment: convertFloat converts the string to a float64value.

nodes.Name: scanComplex
nodes.DocComment:
scanComplex converts the next token to a complex128 value.
The atof argument is a type-specific reader for the underlying type.
If we're reading complex64, atof will parse float32s and convert them
to float64's to avoid reproducing this code for each complex type.

nodes.Name: convertString
nodes.DocComment:
convertString returns the string represented by the next input characters.
The format of the input is determined by the verb.

nodes.Name: quotedString
nodes.DocComment: quotedString returns the double- or back-quoted string represented by the next input characters.

nodes.Name: hexDigit
nodes.DocComment: hexDigit returns the value of the hexadecimal digit.

nodes.Name: hexByte
nodes.DocComment:
hexByte returns the next hex-encoded (two-character) byte from the input.
It returns ok==false if the next bytes in the input do not encode a hex byte.
If the first byte is hex and the second is not, processing stops.

nodes.Name: hexString
nodes.DocComment: hexString returns the space-delimited hexpair-encoded string.

nodes.Name: scanPercent
nodes.DocComment: scanPercent scans a literal percent character.

nodes.Name: scanOne
nodes.DocComment: scanOne scans a single value, deriving the scanner from the type of the argument.

Children.Name: case
Children.RawSource: reflect.Uint, reflect.Uint8, reflect.Uint16, reflect.Uint32, reflect.Uint64, reflect.Uintptr

nodes.Name: errorHandler
nodes.DocComment: errorHandler turns local panics into error returns.

nodes.Name: doScan
nodes.DocComment: doScan does the real work for scanning without a format string.

nodes.Name: advance
nodes.DocComment:
advance determines whether the next characters in the input match
those of the format. It returns the number of bytes (sic) consumed
in the format. All runs of space characters in either input or
format behave as a single space. Newlines are special, though:
newlines in the format must match those in the input and vice versa.
This routine also handles the %% case. If the return value is zero,
either format starts with a % (with no following %) or the input
is empty. If it is negative, the input did not match the string.

nodes.Name: doScanf
nodes.DocComment:
doScanf does the real work when scanning with a format string.
At the moment, it handles only pointers to basic types.
